title_en: Persistence through change by passing on

clauses.en: If from some step on a pattern has at each step something that carries it, and no carrier carries it at two steps d steps apart, then afterwards no d successive steps can all be without a carrier that begins to carry it.

Under passing on: if from some step on a pattern has at each step something that carries it, and no carrier carries it at two steps d steps apart, then from then on any d successive steps include a step at which the pattern passes to a carrier;
If at one step nothing carries the pattern, then at every later step nothing carries it;
If no carrier carries the pattern at two steps d steps apart, and from some step T on the pattern passes to nothing, then from T + d on nothing carries it.
Renewed: for every step, every dependence on this condition at that step is kept across that step.
Restored: for every step, the need of every dependence on this condition at that step is met at some later step.
A return bound is an upper bound on a number of steps: if every dependence is met within p steps after its step, the condition is said to be restored with return bound p.
Restored with return bound zero holds exactly where no relatum depends on the condition.
Consumed: some formation depends on this condition at a step, and at every later step the level of this condition is below the need of that step.
Broken for good: some dependence is broken at a step, and at every later step the level of this condition is below the need of that step.
Every condition broken for good is consumed.
There is a web in which one condition is consumed and no dependence on it is broken.
Every renewed condition is restored with return bound one;
A condition restored with return bound p is likewise restored with every return bound greater than p, and is restored;
A restored condition is not consumed;
A condition is consumed exactly where there is a dependence whose need of its step no later step meets.
There is a condition restored with return bound two, not with return bound one, and not renewed;
There is a condition that is restored and has no return bound.
Renewing: every condition a relatum depends on or draws from at each step is renewed;
Consuming: a relatum at some step draws from a consumed condition.
Every renewing relatum is not consuming, and is admitted at every step.
There is a relatum that is neither renewing nor consuming.

title_en: Renewing and consuming belong to the run

clauses.en: There is a process with two runs from one configuration such that the relatum that draws from a condition is active at every step on both runs, is renewing on one run and consuming on the other, and the formation that depends on the condition is not active on the other run from the first step on.

In a family where giving waits on admission of the dependent (one condition; the formation that depends on it gives it r only at steps at which it is admitted, and the relata that draw from it draw only at steps at which that formation is admitted), with positive need and a starting level not below the need: if two relata that draw from the condition each take no more than r at each step, then each of them, drawing alone, is renewing;

If the two are read together as one joint drawer, and the joint taking exceeds r at each step, then the joint drawer is consuming, and from some step on neither the joint drawer nor the formation that depends on the condition is active.

There is a process such that for every finite bound h there are two runs whose configurations and moves do not differ before h, at every step between which this condition has joint excess, every event of the relatum that draws from it is within renewal (active at its step, and every dependence on each condition it depends on or draws from is kept across that step), and one run is renewing while the other is consuming.
So for this process, every reading fixed by the prefix of the first h steps that includes every renewing run must include a consuming run;
The reading by taking within giving is fixed by the prefix at each step, and does not distinguish the two runs at any uptake before the bound.

Undermining: a relatum draws from a condition at a step, and after the step the level of the condition is both below the need of a dependence at that step and below a need this dependence met at some step from which it has stood without interruption.
Every drawing at whose step a dependence is broken is undermining;
A relatum within renewal at a step does not undermine;
A renewing relatum is within renewal at every step at which it is active.
If a relatum undermines a condition at a step, then some formation has a bearing dependence on this condition at that step, and the events of the two at that step interact (二·十四).

title_en: Renewing and consuming along the continuation relation

clauses.en: Renewing along the continuation relation: every condition that anything continuing a relatum depends on or draws from is renewed;

Consuming along the continuation relation: something continuing a relatum draws from a consumed condition (what continues it: step by step, from what is active before the step to what the continuation relation reads as its continuation and is active after the step, 三·十一).

Undermining along the continuation relation: a relatum draws from a condition at a step, and after the step the level of the condition is both below the need of a dependence at that step and below a need that some formation this dependent formation continues along the continuation relation met at its step (at each step of the continuation relation between, the formations before and after both depend on this condition).

A relatum is renewing along the continuation relation exactly where every condition it depends on or draws from at this step is renewed, and everything active at the next step that the continuation relation reads as its continuation is renewing along the continuation relation: renewing passes into each branch of a split.

A relatum is consuming along the continuation relation exactly where at this step it draws from a consumed condition, or something active at the next step that the continuation relation reads as its continuation is consuming along the continuation relation: if what a merge yields is consuming, each relatum merged into it is consuming.

Under a re-identification that carries its continuation relation with it, what continues a relatum does not change, and renewing, consuming and undermining along the continuation relation do not change.
Reading activity by persists (三·十八), if a re-identification does not change the names of what persists across a step, then for what persists at every step, renewing and consuming do not change.
For a relatum active at every step and continued only by itself, renewing and consuming along the continuation relation from step zero are renewing and consuming;
For what is continued only by itself, undermining along the continuation relation is undermining.
The generative space is the formations that the levels at a step admit (for admission see 二·一).
For every step, if the levels at every condition are not lower than other levels, then they admit everything in the generative space of the other levels.
Includes: one history of levels admits at every step what another history admits.
Exceeds: one history admits at some step something another history does not admit.
Every history of levels includes itself;
If A includes B and B includes C, then A includes C;
A history that includes another is not exceeded by it.

title_en: Widens, narrows, keeps the same, mixed

clauses.en: Widens: includes and exceeds;
Narrows: another history widens it;
Keeps the same: each includes the other;
Mixed: this exceeds that, and that also exceeds this.
Widening cannot be reversed and is transitive;
Widening is not keeping the same, widening is not mixed, and keeping the same is not mixed.

At a step, if every dependence on a condition still stands across the step with its need not decreased, and a history of levels admits after the step every formation that depends on it: if some relatum undermines this condition at that step, then this history exceeds the levels of the web;
If the levels of the web include this history, then no relatum undermines this condition at that step.
There is a world that balances, dissipates and is dependent;

one relatum depends on one condition only, this condition is renewed, fed from beyond and taking within giving, this relatum is active and admitted at every step, and at one step it undermines the condition another relatum depends on, and the other relatum is not active from the second step on.
A part withheld: the members of the part take nothing and give nothing, while the taking and giving outside the part are as before.
The levels under a part withheld are the levels that, from one and the same starting level, change at each step by the taking and giving of the flow with the part withheld;
Where they exist, they are unique.
Under every balance, at each step and each condition: the level plus the cumulative uptake of the part equals the level under the part withheld plus the cumulative replenishment of the part.
Generation is generating, as opposed to degeneration.
A part is generative where the history of levels widens the history of levels with this part withheld;
Degenerative: the history of levels with this part withheld widens the history of levels.
For the generative space, a part being generative, degenerative, keeping the same and mixed are four that do not overlap.
The margin is the amount by which the level with a part withheld exceeds a need.

Under every balance, a formation is admitted at a step exactly where at each of its conditions the need plus the cumulative uptake of the part is no more than the level with the part withheld plus the cumulative replenishment of the part.
The balance is needed only at the conditions of this formation and before this step.
Closing off: the levels with a part withheld admit a formation and the levels do not admit it;
Opening: the levels admit a formation and the levels with the part withheld do not admit it.

Under every balance: if up to a step the cumulative uptake of the part at each condition of a formation is no more than its cumulative replenishment, then where the levels with the part withheld admit this formation, the levels admit it; so closing off needs taking beyond giving;
If the cumulative replenishment is no more than the cumulative uptake, then where the levels admit this formation, the levels with the part withheld admit it; so opening needs giving beyond taking;
If at each step and each condition the part gives no less than it takes, then the history of levels includes the history of levels with the part withheld, and nothing is closed off;
If it gives no more than it takes, then the history of levels with the part withheld includes the history of levels, and nothing is opened;
If what is given exactly equals what is taken, the two histories keep the same.

Under every balance, the history of levels widens the history of levels with a part withheld exactly where: for every formation the levels with the part withheld admit, at each of its conditions the need plus the cumulative uptake of the part is no more than the level with the part withheld plus the cumulative replenishment of the part;

and at some step there is a formation the levels with the part withheld do not admit for which, at each of its conditions, the need plus the cumulative uptake of the part is no more than the level with the part withheld plus the cumulative replenishment of the part.
The balance is needed only at the conditions of each formation and before its step.
Gain: the total level of a family rises across a step.

For every family, if its configurations at the steps from T to T + N are pairwise different, where N is the number of configurations within the total level at T, then between T and T + N there is a step across which it gains.
If a family has novelty from some step on, then gain recurs;
for every bound, the total level being above it recurs.
A net giver: across a step it takes part, and gives to a family more than it takes from the family.
If a family gains across a step, then, counting the rest of the whole, there is a net giver: either the rest of the whole or a formation taking part.

The rest of the whole is a net giver exactly where, over the conditions of the family, the sum of the amounts by which the level after the step plus the joint taking exceeds the level before the step plus the joint replenishment is more than the sum of the amounts by which the level before the step plus the joint replenishment exceeds the level after the step plus the joint taking.
If the flow balances on the family across this step, the rest of the whole is not a net giver.
Under every gainless flow: if a family with distinct members gains across a step, then the rest of the whole is its net giver, or the family is not closed at that step;

If a family has novelty from some step on, then for every family with distinct members that contains its members, it recurs that at some step either the rest of the whole is its net giver or the family is not closed;

If from T on endlessly many formations are each first admitted at a step (admitted for the first time since T), each later one at a later step, each with its dependence and need unchanged and all of its conditions in one family with distinct members: then for this family it recurs that at some step either the rest of the whole is its net giver or the family is not closed.

For every whole of the unfolding whose conditions all lie in one family with distinct members, under a gainless flow, if from step T on the rest of the whole is not its net giver: then after every step from T on there are two steps with one configuration, and from T on there is no novelty.

Under every balance in which only what is active takes, and takes only from what it draws from: if the conditions the members of a part draw from are all renewed, then the history of levels includes the history of levels with the part withheld, and is not widened by it.
Under every balance in which at each step and each condition the part gives no more than it takes;

if a formation depends on a condition at step T, the level of this condition afterwards never reaches its need at T, and the levels with the part withheld admit this formation at some later step at which this dependence still stands with need not less than at T: then the history of levels with the part withheld widens the history of levels.

Under every balance in which only what is active takes, and takes only from what it draws from, and only what is active gives: if no member of the part is active at the first step and none arises, then the history of levels and the history of levels with the part withheld keep the same.

With a reading that reads the formations of this world into that world: if everything the history of levels of this world admits is, as read, admitted by the history of levels of that world, this is called including along the reading;
if that history admits a formation at some step that this history admits at that step under no formation read as it, this is called exceeding along the reading;
where both hold, this is called widening along the reading.
Where the reading reads each formation as itself, widening along the reading is widening.

For every world that grows by new formations and new conditions, with the dependences and needs of the old formations unchanged and the levels of the old conditions as before: under the reading of each old formation as itself in the grown world, the grown world widens along this reading exactly where at some step it admits a new formation;
and compared only on the old formations by the levels of their old conditions, it neither widens nor narrows.

From step T to a later step U, along a continuation relation: if everything admitted at step T has a chain of the continuation relation continuing it to something admitted at step U, this is called including along continuation;
if something admitted at step U is such that nothing continued to it by a chain is admitted at step T, this is called exceeding along continuation;
where both hold, this is called widening along continuation.
Where each continues only itself (T not later than U), including and exceeding along continuation are includes and exceeds by name;
Every re-identification that carries this continuation relation with it does not change widening along continuation;
The more chains the continuation relation has, the easier including is and the harder exceeding is.

Reading (AI, D1, D5): continuing generation is generation whose generated in turn generates: what comes to be keeps, supplements, passes on and creates the conditions of later generation and what generates;
its direction is compared by widening, and what widening records does not exhaust continuing generation (六·十四, 六·十五).
Losing beyond a region: at a step, there is a relatum beyond the region that other levels admit and these levels do not admit.
One history includes another exactly where at every step, within every region, it admits what the other history admits.
At a step: what includes within a region includes within every region inside it;
What loses beyond a region also loses beyond every region inside it;
Nothing is lost beyond the whole of the unfolding.

title_en: Widening is what every weighting shares

clauses.en: For the events of a family, where the events both histories admit all lie in the family and admission is decided: one history widens another exactly where for every positive weighting this history counts more under the weighting than the other;

For every class of orders of alternatives that contains the orders of the positive weightings and each of whose orders ranks every widening history above the history it widens: one history widens another exactly where every order of this class ranks this history above the other, whether the orders are additive or not.
Over listed events: for mixed histories, some positive weighting ranks this one above, and some ranks that one above;
If this includes that and every event in which it has more has weight zero, the two count equally under the weighting;
With one and the same positive weight for every event, the order ranks by the number of events admitted.
The value a model (一·三) gives an item is called its image.
A lumping assigns each item under consideration one value, and puts together those with the same value;
The value an item receives is called its class.
A model is same by class for a lumping where any two items of the same class have the same image.
If a model is same by class for a lumping, it is also same by class for every finer lumping: what the finer lumping puts together, this lumping puts together.
For a lumping that puts everything together, a model same by class for it is exactly a model whose image is the same everywhere.
A law-carrying lumping, for a process, is a lumping under which any two configurations of the same class have outcomes of the same class under one and the same move.

For every process and lumping, there is a law on the classes of the lumping that allows every step of the process through the lumping, exactly where this lumping is a law-carrying lumping for this process.
That the process with classes in place of configurations is a law also holds exactly there.
The process with classes in place of configurations allows every step of the process through the lumping;
Everything that allows every step of the process through the lumping allows every step of the process with classes in place of configurations.

For every law with exactly one move and exactly one next configuration at each configuration, a lumping is a law-carrying lumping for this law exactly where the class of the next configuration is same by class for this lumping.
Generalization fixes, from the values in the data, the values of what is of the same class as the data and is not in them.

Where the data are a family, sameness and difference of class are decided, and the model takes two different values: over the models same by class for this lumping, the values in the data fix the value of an item x exactly where the data contain something of the same class as x.

Where sameness and difference of the items under consideration are decided and the model takes two different values: over every model, the values in the data do not fix the value of any item not in the data.

If g is same by class for a lumping and has the same values as f on the data, then for x of the same class as d in the data, the value of g is the value of f exactly where f has the same value at d and at x.

For every claim built from atoms by true, false, and, or, implies, every and some: if two readings assign to each atom claims that imply each other, then the resulting claims imply each other, with no supposition.
A reading of claims that gives one and the same value to any two claims that imply each other is called same under mutual implication.
Every reading from claims to claims is same under mutual implication exactly where claims that imply each other are one;
That the reading by name is same under mutual implication also holds exactly there;
If the reading by name is so, then every reading of claims is so.
A reading built from relations keeps mutual implication without needing this: what results implies each other, and is not one.

title_en: Laws that commute with a model

clauses.en: A law commutes with a model where, at every configuration, taking its image and then advancing one step, and advancing one step and then taking its image, give the same configuration.
If a model moves every configuration, then for every law that commutes with it, the two runs from a configuration and from its image are never at the same configuration at the same step;
nor is there a step at which every run is at one configuration;
so every law that at some step brings these two runs to one configuration does not commute with this model.
If a law commutes with a model, then on a run from a configuration the model does not move, the model does not move the configuration at any step;
A lumping that puts each configuration together with its image and with nothing else is a law-carrying lumping for this law.
Undecided is a third value besides true and false, below true and false in what is known, which revision has not decided.

For N claims, each stating a formula built from the claims and true and false by not, and, or, speaking only of one another, revised starting from all undecided: from step N on they change no more, and the configuration at step N is the least stillness of these N claims;
If the first claim states true and each later claim negates the one before it, then the first N+1 claims still change from step N to the next step.
If the formulas the claims state contain no term true or false, then at every step of revision every claim is undecided.

If N claims speak only of one another and two-valued revision has no stillness on them, then every stillness of three-valued revision leaves a claim undecided: for a claim that negates itself, two-valued revision changes at every step and three-valued revision is undecided at every step.
The order of steps is the sequence of takings and givings;
The order of steps of a relatum is the sequence of the takings and givings that touch this relatum.
An interleaving combines the orders of steps of the relata into one order of steps: in it, the takings and givings that touch each relatum follow the order of steps of that relatum.

title_en: Takings and givings that touch no relatum in common can exchange their order of steps

clauses.en: If takings and givings change nothing they do not touch, and change what they touch only according to what they touch: where two takings and givings touch no relatum in common, exchanging their order of steps leaves the same configuration after.

If one family contains all the relata, then two families of takings and givings that give every relatum the same order of steps, starting from one and the same configuration, end at one and the same configuration, and each relatum has the same value after each of its takings and givings, in the same sequence;
So two interleavings of the same orders of steps, starting from one and the same configuration, end at one and the same configuration.

title_en: When the orders of steps of the relata fix their interleaving

clauses.en: If takings and givings change nothing they do not touch, change what they touch only according to what they touch, and one family contains all the relata: the orders of steps of the relata fix their interleaving exactly where every taking and giving touches at least one relatum, and every two takings and givings are either the same or touch a relatum in common.

Where sameness of takings and givings is decided, an assignment of an order of steps to each relatum has an interleaving combining them exactly where scheduling them in a number of steps equal to the total number of takings and givings the orders contain can be completed.

If takings and givings change nothing they do not touch, change what they touch only according to what they touch, values of relata are counted in natural numbers, sameness of relata is decided, and one family contains all the relata: in the world an interleaving forms, if the members of this family are distinct, there is balance at every step;
If two adjacent takings and givings that touch no relatum in common exchange their order of steps, the levels of the two worlds differ at most at the one step between them.
For the two worlds formed by two interleavings of the same orders of steps: a property of the level of a relatum holds at some step in this world exactly where it holds at some step in that world;
it holds at every step in this world exactly where it holds at every step in that world.

There is moreover a renumbering of steps such that what reads only the relations among the relata touched by the taking and giving of one step holds alike at this step and its next step in this world and at the renumbered step and its next step in that world;

If every taking and giving of the two interleavings touches at least one relatum, this renumbering is a one-to-one renumbering of the steps within their length, with the renumbering in the other direction as its inverse.

Reading the relations among relata they do not touch can differ with the interleaving: there are two relata, A and B, and two worlds formed by two interleavings of the same orders of steps, such that in one world at some step the level of A is less than that of B, and in the other world at no step.

title_en: What shows is only the order of steps of becoming

clauses.en: An idle step is a step of a reading of steps that reads again the step read before it: the reading starts from the first step, each step either reads again the step read before it or reads the next step, and every step is read.

Where sameness and difference of the relata of a world are decided, read the world with a reading that inserts idle steps: if what takes part at each step is distinct, then balance, dissipation, giving only by what is active, taking only by what is active and only from what it draws from, dependent and embodied each hold of the read world exactly where they hold of the original world, and the uptake and replenishment over any stretch are as over the stretch read;
The rises and falls of any amount and the number of steps at which it rises or falls are as over the stretch read;
Arising recurs, ceasing recurs, and a rise or fall of the level of a relatum recurs, each exactly where it does so in the original world.

If at the idle steps nothing in the world takes part and no relatum changes, and every step read gives the step that is not idle and reads it, then for the world with the idle steps removed, balance, dissipation, giving only by what is active, taking only by what is active and only from what it draws from, dependent and embodied each hold exactly where they hold of the original world;
The uptake and replenishment over any stretch, the rises and falls of the total level of a family, and the number of steps at which they rise or fall, are also the same.
But what each step counts differs with the unit of the reading: read with a reading in which idle steps recur, no flow is more without end;
There is a flow that is more without end, and read twice at each step it is not;
There is a web that a reserve starting at one carries, and read twice at each step, every reserve that carries it starts at no less than two.
What a step touches is the relata touched by the taking and giving of that step.

Where what is touched is given and includes its taking and giving (a relatum not touched does not take part at that step and does not change across it), then over a finite stretch, the renumberings of steps that can be reached by exchanging adjacent takings and givings that are not linked (linked: the two touch a relatum in common, or a relatum one touches depends at the start or end of its step on a relatum the other touches) are exactly those that keep the order of steps of linked takings and givings.
The law of every step: if something is taken from a family, then there is at least one taker, and the number of takers is no more than the total taken from the family;
if something is taken from or given to a family, then at that step some relatum taking part takes or gives.

The form of one step is what a step shows of a family: the levels of the members before and after the step, what is taken from and given to each member, the number of takers, and whether at that step some relatum taking part takes or gives.

Every form of one step is shown by some world at some step on some family (with distinct relata taking part at that step) exactly where it keeps the law of every step: the laws one step shows are exhausted by the law of every step.
It is shown by a family that balances at that step exactly where, in addition, each member balances.
Goes on: there is a run from a configuration: from this configuration on, at every step there is a transition its process allows, running without end.
If a configuration that returns can be reached from a configuration, then that configuration goes on.
If one family contains all the configurations, then a configuration goes on exactly where there is a history from it whose number of steps is the length of the family;
exactly where a configuration that returns can be reached from it.
A horizon is a finite bound: two runs agree up to a horizon where their configurations are the same up to the horizon (inclusive) and their moves are the same before the horizon.

A situation is one of the ways by which a step is taken: counting steps by a weighting, if the weight of a step (from a configuration by a move to a configuration) is k, then this step has k situations, each fixing its own outcome.

title_en: Weighting is the number of situations

clauses.en: For every counting of steps by a weighting: with situations as moves, the process is a law;
this law takes a step exactly where the weight of this step is positive.

If one family contains all the moves and one all the configurations, then the sum of any reading over the histories of situations of n steps equals the sum over the histories of n steps, each counted by its weight (the product of the weights of its steps);

If sameness and difference of moves and of configurations are decided and each occurs once in its family, then the number of histories of situations that take a given history is the weight of this history.

For every assignment of weights to steps (weights of alternatives added, weights of successive steps multiplied, addition and multiplication each keeping its laws), where one family contains all the moves and one all the configurations: the sum over the histories of n steps, each counted by its weight (the weights of its steps multiplied in order, multiplied by what the final configuration reads), is exactly what is computed step by step: from a configuration, multiply the weight of each transition of one step by what follows it and add, computing n steps.

With a reading that sorts the configurations into classes, each class having one configuration as its representative: for every n, what results after n steps is same by class for every reading fixed by class, exactly where what results after one step is same by class for every reading fixed by class.

Rule switching is change by a rule that reads the configuration it is in: in a run of configuration and rule, the configuration changes at each step according to the rule of that step, and the rule changes only at reading steps, according to the configuration and rule of that step, and at the other steps is as before.
A reading step is a step at which the rule reads the configuration.
The fast layer is the layer in which the configuration changes at each step according to the rule.

title_en: The rule meets differences of configuration only at reading steps

clauses.en: For every run of configuration and rule: if there is no reading step before step r, then up to step r (inclusive), two runs starting from one and the same rule have the same rule at every step, whatever their configurations;
At the step after a reading step, the rule is fixed by the configuration and rule of that step.
If the rule never reads, then the rule is at every step as at first, and no difference of configuration reaches the rule;
A configuration that cannot be had at step n under the law that holds this rule fixed is, from step n on, never again a configuration of a run starting from this rule;

If one family contains all the configurations and the law that holds this rule fixed has confluence, then from the step equal to the length of the family on, at every step, not every configuration is the configuration at that step of some run starting from this rule.
There is a run of configuration and rule in which, for two fixed rules, the law that holds each one fixed never reaches a certain configuration from the first step on;
and for the run in which the rule reads the configuration at each step and changes, reaching these two configurations recurs.

title_en: Hexagram, hexagram line, line value, place and halves

clauses.en: A hexagram line is a place of a hexagram with its value;
Line values are the two values of a hexagram line: firm, an undivided line;
yielding, a divided line.
A hexagram is a configuration of six hexagram lines from the bottom up, sixty-four in all.
A place is where a hexagram line stands, six in all from the first to the top.
The halves are the two halves of a hexagram: the lower half from the first to the third, the upper half from the fourth to the top;
Each place is one height of a half, and the heights are low, middle and high.

Under the law of the mutual hexagram, after two steps, the hexagrams whose third and fourth lines are both firm reach Qian, those whose third and fourth lines are both yielding reach Kun, and those whose third and fourth lines differ are drawn into the attractor in which Jiji and Weiji alternate;
Among the sixty-four hexagrams, these number sixteen, sixteen and thirty-two.

title_en: In phase, central place, line correspondence, adjacency, rising seam and riding seam

clauses.en: The parity of places: the first, third and fifth are odd; the second, fourth and top are even.
In phase: the value of a hexagram line agrees with the parity of its place: firm in an odd place, yielding in an even place.
The central places are the second and the fifth, the middle height of the halves.
Line correspondence: the two hexagram lines at the same height of the halves have different values.
A seam is between two adjacent places, five in all.
Adjacency: the two hexagram lines of a seam have different values;
Yielding below and firm above is a rising seam; firm below and yielding above is a riding seam.

title_en: Relations of place are all read in context

clauses.en: Every relation of place, read site by site (place, height, seam), is read in context: what the sites show has gluing into one reading of the whole hexagram exactly where what each site shows agrees.
Taking the halves as two contexts, each showing the hexagram lines of its three heights: the two halves have gluing exactly where no height has line correspondence;
Tai has a height with line correspondence, so for any process, no context-free frame agrees with what the halves show, while a frame that carries contexts agrees with it;
The in-phase readings of the places have gluing exactly at Jiji and Weiji;
The line correspondences of the heights have gluing exactly where all three heights have line correspondence or none has;
The adjacencies of the seams have gluing exactly at Qian, Kun, Jiji and Weiji.
At each step of the waxing-waning ring, the lower five hexagram lines each go up one place, and the top line leaves and, with its line value reversed, becomes the first line;

A line that goes up one place must reverse whether it is in phase, and the line that becomes the first line is in phase or not as before; so the number of lines in phase at the next step differs in parity from that at this step.
The line correspondences of the three heights at the next step are determined by the line correspondences of the three heights at this step;
the number of lines in phase at the next step is not determined by the number of lines in phase at this step.

title_en: Line correspondence is fixed by in phase

clauses.en: For every hexagram: the two hexagram lines of a height have line correspondence exactly where both are in phase or both are not in phase;
If none of the six hexagram lines is in phase, then all three heights have line correspondence.
From the bottom up, the number of rising seams plus the firmness of the first line equals the number of riding seams plus the firmness of the top line (firm counting one, yielding zero).
Taking its complement, every place reverses whether it is in phase, the line correspondence of every height and the adjacency of every seam stay as before, and rising and riding seams exchange;
Taking its turning over, being in phase reverses at the opposite place, line correspondence is kept at the opposite height, and rising and riding seams exchange at the opposite seam.
The waxing-waning ring commutes with the complement;
so the two runs of the waxing-waning ring from a hexagram and from its complement are at no step the same hexagram.

title_en: Fixed phase and holds its place

clauses.en: Fixed phase: only the second to fifth places have a fixed parity; the first and top have none.
Holds its place: a hexagram line is in phase at a place that has fixed phase.

title_en: The first and top have no place

clauses.en: If two hexagram lines have different values at one place, then whatever the parity of this place, one of the two lines is in phase.
The top line of Xu is yielding and the top line of Qian is firm, yet the Xiao Xiang of Xu says it does not hold its place, and the Wenyan of Qian says it has no place;
so no parity of the top place can agree with both statements.
The sentences of the Xiao Xiang that speak of place are collected into a family (the top six of Xu not among them), and all lie in the second to fifth places;
Read by fixed phase, the sentences of the family and the two statements on the top six of Xu and the top nine of Qian all hold.
The in-phase readings of the second to fifth places have gluing exactly where their four hexagram lines all hold their place or none does, eight hexagrams in all.

Reversing the line value of the first or the top line leaves whether each of the second to fifth is in phase as before, while the line correspondence of its height and the adjacency of its seam reverse.
After one step of the waxing-waning ring, whether the second is in phase is fixed by the first line, and the first has no fixed phase;
so whether the second to fifth are in phase at the next step is not determined by whether the second to fifth are in phase at this step.
Sole line: a hexagram line whose value differs from that of each of the other five lines.

A hexagram line is a sole line exactly where it is the only line in the hexagram with its value: the line is firm and the hexagram has only one firm line, or the line is yielding and the hexagram has five firm lines;
A hexagram has a sole line exactly where it has one firm line or five firm lines;
A hexagram has at most one sole line;
A hexagram line is a sole line exactly where reversing its line value makes all six lines the same, twelve hexagrams in all.
If a hexagram has a sole line, then after one step of the waxing-waning ring it has none;
If the sole line is at the top, at the next step it leaves and all six lines are the same, and at the step after that the first line is a sole line.

title_en: What the Xiang and the Tuan say of place

clauses.en: The sentences of the Xiao Xiang that speak explicitly of place are collected into a family (the top six of Xu not among them), and all agree with whether their line is in phase;
The sentences that speak of central and correct are collected into a family (the six in the fifth place of Gen not among them), and all are of lines in a central place and in phase;
The sentences that speak of the yielding riding the firm are collected into a family, and in all of them the seam below their line is a riding seam.
The hexagrams of which the Tuan says "the firm is central and responded to" are collected into a family, and all have a firm line in a central place and line correspondence at the middle height.

title_en: The sequence of the Xugua as a run of a law

clauses.en: For every law under which, in a family, the outcome of each member other than the last is the member after it, and which commutes with a model that is its own inverse (the image of its image is the item itself): if in the family a member is followed by its image and the image by t, then t is this member.
The sequence of the Xugua starts from Qian and has each of the sixty-four hexagrams once, in order;

Every law whose run from Qian follows this sequence commutes with none of the three models complement, turning over, and complement of the turning over: in the sequence Qian is followed by Kun (Kun is the complement of Qian, and also the complement of its turning over) and Kun by Zhun, and Zhun is followed by Meng (Meng is the turning over of Zhun) and Meng by Xu, and neither returns to the hexagram before it.
There is a law whose run from Qian follows this sequence.
Couples into: a condition goes into a formation: if a formation depends on a condition at some step, then this condition couples into it by the threshold of its need;
or, given separately, it couples into it by its level; this is given separately and does not change with the step.
Coupling has a direction, from the condition into the formation.

title_en: Selection, selector and selection through couplings

clauses.en: Selection is any claim about histories of levels: what remains, what is rewarded, what leaves more after it.

Two histories of levels are alike through the couplings of a formation at a step where the levels of this step both admit it or both do not admit it, and every condition that couples into it by its level has the same level in both.
Selection through couplings: any two histories alike through the couplings of the selector up to some step are treated the same by the selection.
The selector is the formation to which the couplings that a selection goes through belong.
Reading (AI, D45): own course through couplings is the further course of a formation itself, fixed by the lumping that its couplings make.

Where sameness and difference of conditions are decided: if a condition couples into a formation only by threshold, the other conditions coupling into it have the same levels at a step, and the two levels of this condition at this step both meet its need or both do not, then the two histories are alike through its couplings at this step.
If what couples in by level is enlarged, two histories alike up to some step through the enlarged couplings are also alike through the couplings before enlargement.
Coupling read early: a condition couples into a formation by its level, and a difference in its level is separated by the couplings of the formation at that very step.

Wherever a condition couples into a formation by its level, if two histories of levels differ in its level at some step, then the two histories are not alike through the couplings of the formation at that step.
A feature assigns each configuration one value.
For every reading of a feature through a lumping, what is read is single-valued exactly where the feature is same by class for its lumping.
For every family of configurations, with some value given: there is a reading that reads only the class and gives the feature of each member, exactly where the feature is same by class on the family;
If the lumping puts together two members of the family with different features, there is no such reading.
Upstream of c are the conditions from which a chain of couplings leads to c;
Downstream of c are the conditions to which a chain of couplings leads from c (the chain may have length zero).
Observation is a route of readings starting from what is observed: a route of length zero is direct witness, the others are received by passing on.
For every law that reads, at each condition, the levels it marks, all the marked conditions lying in one family;

if two flows both balance, the formations taking part are the same, the moves of the part are the same, the formations outside the part all follow this law, and at the start only the level of one condition differs: then at each step, for every condition not downstream of this condition (counting by the routes of reading formed by this step), the levels of the two flows are the same.
The routes of reading formed by the next step are exactly the routes formed by this step together with those extended by a coupling at this step.
Every route newly formed by the next step goes through a coupling at this step.

An example: from some step on, a formation adds at each step the level of one condition to another condition (the recorded one), and at each step at which the recorded one is not less than a certain number, takes one from the former;
at this step, the route from the former to the recorded one forms;
if two flows differ only in the level of the former, then up to this step the recorded ones are the same, and across this step the recorded ones come to differ by the gap of the former.
Reached by in time: at some step within the time limit, some relatum the source can reach couples into what reads at that step.
What the source can reach is formed only by the following three: a relatum already reached is still reached at the next step;
if the source touches a relatum at a step, the relatum is reached at the next step;
if a relatum is already reached at some step and at that step couples into a formation, and this formation at that step or some later step touches a relatum, that relatum is reached at the next step.

title_en: Not reached, the answers are the same

clauses.en: For every two histories: their starting levels are the same;
before the time limit there is balance at every step, and what takes part is the same;
apart from the source, every formation before the time limit takes and gives the same wherever the two histories are alike through its couplings up to that step;
the answer is read only through the couplings of what reads up to the time limit.
Then every relatum not yet reached by the source at a step within the time limit has the same level at that step;
if the source has not reached what reads by the time limit, the two histories are alike through the couplings of what reads up to the time limit, and the two answers are the same.
So if the two answers differ, then reached by in time cannot be refuted;
if reached by in time is decided, then it holds.
Sensitive: the taking and giving of a formation at some step is not fixed by the levels of the other conditions up to that step alone; the formation is then called sensitive to this condition.

Where sameness and difference of conditions are decided: for every law of taking and giving under which the conditions read at each step, for each formation and each history, all lie in one family, for each formation outside the part, if two histories agree up to some step on admission at every step and on the levels of the conditions it is sensitive to, then the law gives the same taking and giving at this step;

For every relation of coupling by level that, put in place of sensitivity, keeps the previous sentence true, that each condition a formation outside the part is sensitive to couples into this formation cannot be refuted.

The weak limited principle of omniscience holds exactly where: for every run of a process, what is read step by step along it as holding or not either fails at every step, or it is not the case that it fails at every step.

With conditions numbered by natural numbers: there are a law of taking and giving that reads only what is already settled and a formation such that two histories agree up to some step on the conditions this formation is sensitive to while the taking and giving the law gives this formation at this step still differ, exactly where there is a model that fixes, for every step-by-step sequence of holding or not, whether it fails at every step;
If there is such a model, then the weak limited principle of omniscience holds.
Testing: if no history of levels that satisfies a claim is alike with what holds through the couplings of a formation up to some step, then this claim is excluded for this formation at this step.
A claim is excluded only through differences that couple in: if a history satisfying this claim is alike with what holds through its couplings up to this step, then this claim is not excluded here.
A claim that what holds satisfies is not excluded;
once excluded, it is excluded at every later step;
If what couples in by level is enlarged, what is excluded is still excluded.
Every selection through the couplings of a formation up to some step selects two histories alike exactly where the two histories are alike through its couplings up to this step;
If two histories are not alike through its couplings up to this step, then some selection through its couplings holds of this one and not of that one.
The admission of this formation at this step and at any step before it is a selection through its couplings up to this step.
A selection through the couplings of a selector is excluded at the selector under a history exactly where it does not hold of this history.
If what couples in by level is enlarged, a selection through couplings is still through couplings.
Where couplings are read as values, two histories are alike through its couplings up to some step exactly where the prefixes of its own course up to this step are the same;
a selection through its couplings is exactly a selection by this prefix;
If under the two histories its own course has no more than N and N′ configurations respectively, then two histories alike through its couplings before step N + N′ − 1 are alike at every step.

Where sameness and difference of conditions are decided: without admitted histories, a finite prefix does not exclude what comes after: at any step, the two claims "some condition eventually reaches zero" and "after this step it is above zero at every step" are not excluded for any formation under any relation of coupling by level.
Being excluded within the admitted histories is exactly the exclusion of the claim "lies in the admitted histories and satisfies this claim".
An example: the admitted histories do not contain what holds, a claim that what holds satisfies is excluded at the first step, and what couples in excludes these admitted histories at the next step.

Taking the histories of levels of a flow under balance as the admitted histories, with what holds among them, and a condition coupling into a formation by its level, the false claim "this condition eventually reaches zero" is excluded at the first step.
Testing is relative to the formation.
An example: a claim is excluded at no step for one formation, and is excluded at the third step for another formation.
An example: a claim is not excluded for either of two formations, and is excluded when tested by the couplings of the two together.
A judgment process ends, at the configuration judged, with an answer that can be allowed.
An answer is a common answer of the judgment process exactly where it can be allowed at every configuration in doubt;
If what is in doubt narrows, a common answer is still a common answer.

For a judgment process through the couplings of a formation, taking as what is in doubt the histories alike with what holds through its couplings, its common answer is exactly an answer that can be allowed at every one of these histories.
The scope of knowing is what an inquiry tree, actually executed from the configurations in doubt, reaches.
Everything in the scope of knowing is reached from a configuration in doubt by an actual path of the process.
An inquiry tree whose questions can all be allowed, whose answers are all common answers, and which aborts only when what is in doubt is empty, meets the target throughout its scope of knowing;
If what this inquiry tree has in doubt contains a configuration, then its scope of knowing contains a configuration that meets the target.

A prefix (五·六) fixes the outcome of a move at a configuration as a certain configuration where every law that allows each transition of this run before this step sends this configuration by this move to that configuration.
If a run has taken a move at a configuration before this step, the prefix fixes its outcome.
For every process that is a law, where there are two different configurations: if a run has not taken a move at a configuration before this step, the prefix does not fix its outcome;
For a run of kept history, at every configuration it passes through, the prefix fixes only the outcomes of the moves it took.
A counterfactual is the history produced when the move of a part differs from the move it took and the rest follow one and the same law.

Where the rest follow a law of taking and giving that reads only what is already settled: if two flows both balance, what takes part is the same, the moves of the part are the same and the starting levels are the same, then the levels and every taking and giving of the two flows at each step are the same.

For every law of taking and giving that reads only what is already settled, the flow it produces balances on the levels it produces exactly where its history can be run: at no step is more taken from a condition than its level plus what is given to it.

If the moves of the part also follow a law of taking and giving that reads only what is already settled, and the history the two laws produce together can be run: then for every flow under balance in which what takes part is the same as here, the moves of the part are the same as here, the rest follow the former law and the starting levels are the same as here, its levels and takings and givings at each step are the levels and takings and givings of this history;
The same holds where every formation follows a law and the history can be run.
So the counterfactual of a move is the history this move produces.

For every law and a run of it: the law has a step from a configuration by a move beyond the law shown by this run exactly where the law has a step from this configuration by this move and the run never took this move at this configuration.

With the moves of the part as inputs and the rest following a law of taking and giving, the history of a run is a consistent history, and the part has a step by a move at a configuration beyond what this history shows exactly where this run never took this move at this configuration: what the law adds to its history is exactly its counterfactuals.
An experiment changes its own move where the configuration returns.
If a run at some step returns to the configuration of an earlier step and takes a move, then from the next step on, the prefix fixes the outcome of this move at this configuration.

For every process that is a law, where there are two different configurations: if the configurations of a run have no return, then at every configuration it passes through, the prefix does not fix the outcome of any move other than the one it took.
If the classes of the configurations of a run all lie in one family, then after every step there are two steps with the same class.
Control: every step of a process through a lumping is a step of one process: the given control says that what the lumping puts together is irrelevant to the change.

If every step of a process through a lumping is a step of a law, the outcome of a move at a class fixed by the prefix through this lumping is the class of the outcome of this move at every configuration of this class, whether or not the run passes through it.
An example: a hidden factor that the lumping puts together changes at every step, and the move changes nothing: through this lumping the prefix fixes two moves that differ nowhere to two outcomes;

If the move changes along with the hidden factor the lumping puts together, then the wrong law "the move fixes its outcome" allows at every step the steps read through this lumping, and the prefix never excludes it;
If the move is changed against the hidden factor the lumping puts together, then by the fifth step no law allows the steps it reads.
A record is the note of what occurs in one occasion;
A dated record notes what was asked and what was answered on one day.
Retrodiction reads, from later dated records, the contents of an earlier package.
Every history that holds agrees with what its own records answered.

Reading the contents of an earlier package: where sameness and difference of answers and contents are decided, for a region of histories, every history that agrees with what each record answered and gives the same package as an admitted hidden source gives the contents that hold, exactly where every history of this region that gives the same package as an admitted hidden source but different contents has a dated record on which its answer differs from what holds.
If the records at the two ends show a change, then for each day between, there is a course that has already changed at it and a course that has not yet changed at it, each with only one change.
A run adheres to a reading: for every finite stretch of it, some run of this reading agrees with it up to this stretch.
A run adheres to a reading exactly where every closed class of histories that contains the runs of this reading contains it.
A reading can be refuted where every run not in it has a finite stretch such that every run agreeing with it up to this stretch is not in it.
For a reading that can be refuted, that every run adhering to it lies within the reading cannot be refuted;
For every process, every reading that can be refuted contains the runs that adhere to it, exactly where double-negation stability holds for every claim.

For the process with one configuration and one move, for every step-by-step sequence of holding or not, take the history of all the stretches before the step at which it first holds: for every such sequence, this history either has a latest stretch or has stretches beyond every horizon, exactly where the limited principle of omniscience holds.
A reading is called dense where for every finite stretch some run of the reading agrees with it up to this stretch;

There is something that for every run and every horizon puts down a reading, what it puts down fixed only by the prefix up to this horizon, every reading it puts down lying within one reading and containing a run that agrees with this run up to this horizon, exactly where this reading is dense.
Verification: a run has a stretch such that every run agreeing with it up to this stretch lies within a reading.
Where every run within a reading has such a stretch, the reading is called verifiable;
A reading is verifiable exactly where each of its runs is verified within it.
A run lies within a reading exactly where it adheres to this reading and, if it adheres, lies within it;
No finite stretch can refute "if it adheres, it lies within it".
Asked of every process: if the complement of every verifiable reading can be refuted, then Markov's principle holds;

and Markov's principle holds exactly where: for every run of a process with each step marked as holding or not, the mark of each step fixed only by the prefix up to this step, every run that is not marked as not holding at every step has a step such that every run agreeing with it up to this step is not marked as not holding at every step.
A method answers "yes" or "no" at each horizon of each run.
A method verifies in the limit a reading where this reading holds exactly on the runs on which the method from some step on always answers "yes";
A method refutes a reading in the limit where this reading holds exactly on the runs on which a "yes" of the method recurs.
Where sameness and difference of configurations are decided, the method "nothing changed at the last step" verifies in the limit "the configuration of the run changes no more from some step on".
For a process on two configurations that allows every transition, "the configuration of the run changes no more from some step on" can be neither verified nor refuted;
If Markov's principle holds, no method fixed by prefixes can refute it in the limit.
Identification in the limit is tracking something that does not change with the horizon.
Cross-checking is testing by checking fallible witnesses against one another.

For every two candidates that differ in their answer, no record the witnesses report is admitted by both, exactly where their envelopes are apart: for every fault set of this one and every fault set of that one, some witness is left outside both.
If a candidate that admits all witnesses being faulty is in a run, it stays there forever, and after it no certificate can be established.
Listing the family of witnesses twice changes no step and no certificate.
Silence: giving no value where the value cannot be determined.
Where every value a reading gives on a region is the value of the feature, the reading is said to accord on the region;
Where it gives the value of the feature at every configuration of the region, it is said to hit at every configuration of the region.
What keeps silence everywhere accords on the region;
If the region has a configuration, what keeps silence everywhere does not hit at every configuration of the region.
A reading that accords on the region must keep silence wherever the lumping puts together two configurations of the region with different features.
A reading that hits at every configuration of the region requires the feature to be same by class on the region;

If for each value of the lumping on the region a configuration of the region giving this value is given, then a reading that hits at every configuration of the region exists exactly where the feature is same by class on the region.

title_en: A reading does not exhaust what it reads

clauses.en: For every family of readings indexed by what is read, if there is a model that moves every value, then there is a reading that no reading of the family expresses.
Claims indexed by what is read cannot express every kind of claim;
In a frame whose claims are its own configurations, not every kind of claim about configurations is what some configuration holds.

Where sameness and difference of values are decided and what is read and the values are both nonempty: there is a family of readings indexed by what is read that expresses every reading by comparison for equality, exactly where the values are of only one kind.

For readings indexed by what is read that supply step by step what they lack, each step keeping what the step before expressed and expressing what the step before lacked: if the model used moves every value, then each step lacks its own lack, and a later step must express what an earlier step did not;
If the relation comparing the values is moreover symmetric and transitive, then no finitely many readings can have at every step one of them that expresses what this step lacks.
Extrapolation gives a value from the prefix, or keeps silence.
Hits: it gives a value, and it is the value that comes;
Misses: it gives a value, and what comes differs;
Accords: at no step a miss.
Where sameness and difference of values are decided, a value given that is not a miss is the value that comes: what accords at each step either keeps silence or hits.

title_en: The prefix does not fix what comes, and the diagonal course

clauses.en: A lasso: a course that from some step on returns every fixed number of steps.
For every course and every step, where there are two values, there are two courses with the same prefix as it that take one value each at this step, and both courses are lassos;
It is not so that a value given from this prefix misses on neither course;
Where sameness and difference of values are decided, it misses on one of them.

A diagonal course is a course on which every value an extrapolation gives misses: if there is a model that moves every value, then every value any extrapolation gives on its diagonal course misses, and there is no step from which it hits at every step;
The diagonal course is the course through a model of the trajectory of a law whose configurations contain the whole prefix, and no family contains all its configurations.
Extrapolation by elimination uses candidates in order, moving to the next when the current one misses, and the value it gives is the value the current one gives.
Where sameness and difference of values are decided: the position of the current candidate in the order does not decrease;
Extrapolation by elimination does not pass beyond any candidate that accords with the course;
If some candidate accords with the course, missing does not recur;
Every candidate passed over has missed at some step of the prefix.

For every law all the configurations of whose trajectory lie in one family, the course through any lumping is a lasso, and its start step plus the number of steps of its return is no more than the number of members of the family.

Where sameness and difference of values are decided, on the trajectory of this law, extrapolation by elimination over lasso candidates: its misses are fewer than the triangular number of the number of members of the family;
from the step equal to the number of members of the family on, it gives a value at every step;
missing does not recur;
that from some step on it hits at every step cannot be refuted;
If the number of members of the family is N and its triangular number is T, then from step N + (N + N − 1)·T on it hits at every step.
If extrapolation by elimination over lasso candidates hits at every step from some step on, then the course is a lasso;
If there is a model that moves every value, then its diagonal course is not a lasso.

title_en: Bounded, the prefix fixes the run

clauses.en: For every two courses, one with no more than N kinds of configuration and the other with no more than N′ kinds, if they are the same before step N + N′ − 1, then they are the same everywhere: the prefix up to there fixes them.
This length is exact: where there are two values, for any bounds there are two courses, each with configurations within its bound, the same before step N + N′ − 2 and different at this step.
Where sameness and difference of values are decided, on a course with no more than N kinds of configuration, a lasso candidate within the bound that has no miss before step N + N − 1 never misses.

Where sameness and difference of values are decided, extrapolation that is given no bound and uses the least bound hits at every step from step N + N − 1 on, on every course with no more than N kinds of configuration;
Where there are two values, no extrapolation hits at step M + M + 2 on every course with no more than M + 2 kinds of configuration.

Under a law, where the configurations of a family form an absorbing region of this law, two configurations of the family have the same course through a lumping exactly where their courses are the same before the step equal to the number of members of the family minus one;

Where one family contains all the configurations, this also holds exactly where, from the two configurations themselves, every string of moves can be run alike and the claims that can hold after running are the same.

Training is selection through the data: for every amount computed from the values in the data (two functions the same on the data have the same amount), the selection made from it is the same for two functions the same on the data.
For every region of functions, any two functions in it that are the same on the data have the same value at an input exactly where the data fix the value at this input on this region;
If the region is free at an input outside the data, then every selection through the data is still as free there as the region.

Learnable: for a feature through a lumping, there is an extrapolation that gives values from the prefix through this lumping and, on the trajectory of every configuration, hits at every step from some step on.

Where sameness and difference of classes are decided, in a world whose configurations one family contains: a feature is learnable through a lumping exactly where for any two configurations with the same course through this lumping, their features are the same from some step on;
also exactly where there is a guess fixed only by the prefix through the lumping that tracks this feature in the limit.
Every feature same by class is learnable;
Under a law that leaves every configuration unchanged, the learnable features are exactly those same by class.
If two configurations with the same course through the lumping have features that differ recurrently, then no extrapolation hits at every step from some step on, on both trajectories.
An example: a world of one configuration and one class value, in which each of two features has an extrapolation that hits it at every step from some step on, and no extrapolation does so for both.
Runs part: the classes of two runs are the same before some step and differ at this step.
Wherever runs part, no extrapolation hits on both runs at this step.

For a process whose moves and configurations each have a family containing all of them, where whether a step is allowed is decided and sameness and difference of classes are decided: the extrapolation built from this process hits at some step on every run from a configuration exactly where no two runs from this configuration part at this step.
Where there are two values, after every prefix, in a process in which every configuration can go to every configuration, there are two runs with this prefix that part here.
Typicality: the histories that are the majority by counting show their weighting.
For two values with natural-number weightings p and q, if each history of n steps counts its squared deviation by its weighting, the sum is exactly n·p·q·(p + q)^n;
The sum of the weightings of the histories whose squared deviation is not less than d, multiplied by d, is no more than this number.
For every u not less than v, the sum of the weightings of the histories with at least k ones, multiplied by u^k·v^n, is no more than (p·u + q·v)^n·v^k.
With situations as moves, the number of histories of situations of n steps whose history has a squared deviation not less than d, multiplied by d, is also no more than n·p·q·(p + q)^n.
A name (一·二十) is in three places: the name of a relatum, by which the world labels its relata;
the name of a configuration, the value a reading gives a configuration (the earlier segment of the course of a configuration through a lumping is one kind of it, 十·十);
the name of a sense entry, what a code assigns.
A code assigns names to sense entries;
A sense entry is one meaning a name can refer to;
Hearing: a hearer, for a sense entry, takes the name of the speaker according to whether it follows or not;
A record (九·二十二), for a name, notes whether the name occurs in it and which sense entries it offers.
Under every re-identification, whether each condition is renewed, consumed or broken for good does not change.

Names have no fixed fit: names carry no relation: under every renaming, the renewing, consuming and undermining of a formation, the forming and dissolving of its dependences, its arising, and the web being unceasing do not change;
Replacing the names of a reading or a code by a renaming that merges nothing, whether the reading carries a law and whether the code assigns one name to two sense entries (十·七) do not change.

There is a web with a re-identification under which the relations at every step are the same, while renewing, undermining, forming and unceasing all change, and after the re-identification nothing is renewing and two are consuming.
The law of descriptions that make sense (一·二十三): every two descriptions that make sense put together the same things.
Naming configurations by themselves is a description that makes sense exactly where alike configurations are in fact one.

Where a law is shown through a lumping, if what a reading puts together shows the same, this reading carries the law, and this reading puts together every two configurations that from themselves on show the same at every step, then this reading is a description that makes sense.
A proper name: within one step a name belongs to one relatum only.
An unrestricted name is a name that puts together everything read as one.
Under every re-identification, the new names at each step are proper names.
Every move is same by class for the lumping that names configurations by themselves.
The unrestricted name carries a law for every process;
Where a law is shown through a lumping, the unrestricted name is a description that makes sense exactly where every two configurations from themselves on show the same at every step.
Cross-situational standing: every record in which a name occurs offers the sense entry.
A sense entry lacks cross-situational standing for a name exactly where some record in which this name occurs does not offer it.
Resolves: in a family of sense entries, only one sense entry is left that still has cross-situational standing for a name.

For every family of sense entries with distinct members, where sameness and difference of sense entries are decided: a name resolves to a sense entry exactly where this sense entry is in the family, every record in which this name occurs offers it, and each other sense entry of the family has a record in which this name occurs that does not offer it.
Later records only reduce the members of the family that still have standing; those removed do not return.
If what is meant is in the family and every record in which this name occurs offers it, then the one member of the family that still has standing is what is meant.
Tells apart: a code does not assign one name to two sense entries.
Decodes: the name the code of what reads assigns to a sense entry is exactly the name heard.

For every code of what reads that tells apart: the name the speaker assigns to some sense entry is read as this sense entry and only this exactly where the two codes give this sense entry the same name;
Where what reads assigns the name of the speaker to another sense entry, it decodes it as the other sense entry and not as this one.
A code decodes its own names exactly where it tells apart.
What is same by class on a region for the lumping of one name, reading another name alongside, is also same by class on this region for the lumping of the two names read together.
Code acquisition is obtaining a code by reading what is asked.

For formulas built from two atoms by joining and doubling: for codes in which the values of the two atoms differ, the code read out from what is asked of the two atoms and of one join is the code itself, with the same value on every formula, with no limit of depth;

For codes in which the values of the two atoms differ, reading only the values of the two atoms, the order of joining is not same by class for its lumping, so no reading obtains its order for every one of these codes.

title_en: Prefix names and the values they carry

clauses.en: A prefix name takes the earlier segment of the course of a configuration through a lumping as the name of the configuration.

For every law whose configurations one family of N members contains, where sameness and difference of classes are decided: a feature is learnable through this lumping exactly where there is a family of no more than N members, each member a prefix name (of length N − 1) with the value it carries, such that extrapolation by this family hits, on the trajectory of every configuration, at every step from some step on.

For every extrapolation by a family that hits at every step from some step on, on the trajectory of a configuration, from this step on every value the feature takes is the value carried by some member of the family.
A shared code is a code formed among formations by hearing.
No hearing coins a name: after hearing, the name of each formation for each sense entry is either its old name or the name of the speaker.

If the formations of a region have the same name for a sense entry, and in every hearing on this sense entry in which the hearer is within the region the speaker is also within the region, their sameness does not change.
If all formations have the same name for a sense entry, then afterwards, under every hearing and every following or not, the name of this sense entry does not change.
Where every hearing follows: the name each formation obtains for a sense entry is the name, at the starting point, of its provenance;

Where there are two different names, an order of hearing brings the formations to the same name for this sense entry from every starting point exactly where it brings them to the same provenance for this sense entry;
Where one family contains all the formations and there are formations, the names an order can make shared are exactly the names already in use at the starting point.

For every law of codes unchanged by the exchange of the formations it exchanges and by the renaming of the names it changes, where this renaming moves every name for a sense entry: from a starting point symmetric under both, the exchanged formations never have the same name for this sense entry.
There are two formations for which one that all follow, a preferred name, and an order of hearing each bring them to the same name in one step;
The one that all follow and the order of hearing break the exchange of formations; the preferred name breaks the renaming.

For every hearing that is followed, a code of the hearer that told apart before still tells apart after, exactly where the name taken is not one the hearer has already assigned to another sense entry.

There are two codes, each telling apart two sense entries; one hears the name of the other for one sense entry and follows it, and so assigns one name to two sense entries: sameness of names formed sense entry by sense entry can merge sense entries.
An imposed code is a code put on the formations.
Under every imposed code, the formations have the same name for each sense entry;
