The formations decode one another on every sense entry (decoding it as this and only this) exactly where the code put on them tells apart;
Each formation loses exactly what its original code told apart and the code put on it merges; one whose code is the code put on it loses nothing;
Afterwards no hearing and no following or not changes this.
A distinction merged: if the code is put on the formations of a region, and formations outside the region also hold the names put on, it never returns;

Where the code put on merges two sense entries, if a formation holding the name put on for one of them hears, for the other, a name held that is not the one put on and follows it, it tells these two sense entries apart again.
Each cohort reads the records of the cohort before: if they resolve, then the records of this cohort are a single record in which this name occurs and which offers only the sense entry resolved to;
if they do not resolve, they are passed on as they are.

For every family of sense entries with distinct members, where sameness and difference of sense entries are decided, if the records of the cohort before resolve to a sense entry: from the next cohort on the records change no more, and every cohort resolves to this sense entry.
Two families of records that resolve to the same sense entry become one at the next cohort, and afterwards every reading gives them the same value.
Records that keep the records of the earlier cohort and read the later records together with them only resolve to the original sense entry or do not resolve;
Where records only grow, what they resolve to can be lost but not replaced.

Responds to: the taking and giving of a formation differs with the level of a condition: there are two histories, the same except for the level of some condition at some step, and the law of taking and giving makes the gap between the takings and givings of this formation at a condition across a step positive.

A law of taking and giving reads through couplings where, for every formation outside the part, if two histories are alike through its couplings at every step up to some step, then the taking and giving of this law for this formation across this step do not differ.

title_en: Coupling bounds response and does not fix it

clauses.en: Where for each formation, each step and each history, whether it is alike through couplings with a history is decided, and a formation separates these two histories through its couplings up to some step: then for any condition there is a law of taking and giving that reads through the couplings of all formations under which the uptake of this formation at this condition across this step differs under the two histories;
There is also a law of taking and giving that reads through the couplings of all formations whose taking and giving do not differ at any step or under any history.

title_en: Where coupling by level comes from

clauses.en: For every law of taking and giving that reads through couplings with couplings only by threshold (no condition couples into any formation by its level), where a formation outside the part neither takes nor gives at steps at which the levels do not admit it: if two histories are the same before a step, and at this step the level of each condition in the latter is not less than in the former, then the uptake and the replenishment of this formation at each condition across this step are, in the latter, not less than in the former.

So, where sameness and difference of conditions are decided, for a response whose amount given to a condition is fixed only by the level of condition d at its step, the level of d being no more than N: there is a family of such formations, following such laws, whose sum of giving is exactly this response, exactly where for every x less than N, the response when the level of d is x is no more than when it is x plus one;
No family of such formations has a sum of giving exactly equal to the response that supplies the shortfall of the level of d below a positive amount (N being positive).

Where sameness and difference of conditions are decided and the sum of the levels of d and one other condition at its step is fixed at N, there is a family of formations, each with needs at d and at this condition and neither taking nor giving at steps at which the levels do not admit it, following such laws, whose sum of giving is exactly every response fixed only by the level of d.

Where sameness and difference of conditions and formations are decided, that a condition couples into a formation outside the part by its level cannot be refuted, exactly where it cannot be refuted that there is a law of taking and giving that reads through couplings and responds to it by a change of level that does not change whether the need of this formation at this condition is met.

title_en: What a part reaches and the closures

clauses.en: If a member of a part takes part at some step and takes from or gives to a condition that a formation depends on, the part is said to reach that formation; this is what a part reaches.

The feeding closure is what is contained in common by every region that contains this formation and is such that "if a member of it depends on a condition at some step, and something taking part at this step gives to the condition, then what gives to it is also in it".
The influence closure is what is contained in common by every region that contains this formation and contains everything that takes from or gives to a condition that a member of it depends on.

The reach closure is what is contained in common by every region that contains this formation and is such that "if a condition that a member of it takes from or gives to is depended on by a formation, then this formation is also in it".
The coupling closure is what is contained in common by every region that contains this formation and contains everything that takes from or gives to a condition that couples into a member of it.

The system closure is what is contained in common by every region that contains this formation and contains everything that shares a condition with a member of it (each either depending on it or taking from or giving to it).
The feeding closure lies within the influence closure, and the influence closure within the coupling closure;
The influence closure and the reach closure both lie within the system closure.
Where coupling is only by threshold, the coupling closure is the influence closure.
If B is in the system closure of A, then A is in the system closure of B.
Everything beyond the influence closure takes from and gives to no condition that anything in the closure depends on;
Everything beyond the feeding closure, taking part at any step, gives zero to the conditions that what is in the closure depends on at this step;
Everything beyond the coupling closure takes from and gives to no condition that couples into anything in the closure.

Under every flow that balances, if all members of the part are beyond the influence closure of this formation: then each formation in the influence closure is, at each step, admitted by the levels exactly where it is admitted by the levels with this part withheld (the levels with the part withheld change, from one and the same starting level, at each step by the flow in which the taking and giving of the members of the part are all zero and the rest is as before).
The coupling closure grows with what couples in by level, and also with what takes from or gives to conditions.

If some links are removed from a relation, the closures along it all stay as before exactly where, for every link removed, its end still lies in the closure of its start along the remaining links: every removed link has a bypass.

For a relation grown by attachment (its links a family, each new link joining a relatum not before in any link to another relatum), removing any one of its links separates its two ends: one is not in the closure of the other along the remaining links.

If a relation grown by attachment is joined by one more link, removing a link of the grown relation leaves the closures as before exactly where the two ends of the new link lie on the two sides of this link: along the remaining links, one end of this link reaches one end of the new link, and the other end of the new link reaches the other end of this link.

For a world grown by attachment (its conditions growing one after another, each condition shared by exactly two formations, one of which before this shared no condition), every condition of it is indispensable: the two formations that depend on it or take from or give to it are in one system closure, and along the other conditions alone they are not.

The responsive reach is what is reached, starting from the members of the part, by adding again and again a formation whenever something in it, in either of two flows, takes from or gives to a condition that couples into this formation.
A formation is in the responsive reach of the part exactly where some member of the part is in the coupling closure this formation has through the two flows.
The selection gap is what lies in the reach closure of a formation and not in its coupling closure.

If the conditions coupling into everything in the coupling closure of this formation balance at every step, and all members of the part are beyond its coupling closure: then every selector through the couplings of anything in the coupling closure (this formation included) selects the history of levels and the history of levels with this part withheld alike;
For any region all of whose members lie in its coupling closure, what selects through the couplings of all its members together also selects them alike.

If the rest follow, in both flows, a law of taking and giving that reads through couplings, both flows balance, what takes part is the same, the starting levels are the same, and the part moves alike within the coupling closure this formation has through the two flows (if the members of the part in the closure are alike through couplings up to some step, their takings and givings across this step at conditions coupling into anything in the closure do not differ): then every selector through the couplings of anything in this closure selects the histories of levels of the two flows alike;
The consequence of the move (the selection that holds with this move and does not hold without it) is at no step a selection through the couplings of anything in this closure.

If the law of the rest and the laws of the two moves read only what is already settled, the first move reads through the couplings of the members of the part, the two moves do not differ at conditions coupling into anything in the closure, and both histories can be run: then the same holds of the two histories, with nothing given separately.

If two flows each balance at a condition c at every step: whether the level of c is the same in the two flows changes only across steps at which the joint taking or the joint replenishment of the two flows at c differ;
If what takes part is the same, then at this step some formation taking part must take from or give to c differently in the two flows.

If the levels of the two histories at c become the same again at a step (coming together again), then from any earlier step to this step, the takings and givings of the two flows at c exactly make up their gap: the level of one flow at the earlier step plus what is given in it in between plus what the other flow takes in between equals the level of the other flow at the earlier step plus what is given in it in between plus what this flow takes in between.

If the rest follow, in both flows, a law of taking and giving that reads through couplings, what takes part is the same, and from some step on the part takes from and gives to c the same in both flows: then every later change in whether the level of c is the same must go through a formation taking part outside the part whose taking and giving at c across some step differ in the two flows, while the histories of levels of the two flows are not alike through its couplings up to that step.

title_en: Raising what is coupled draws from beyond

clauses.en: Under every flow that balances, where sameness and difference of conditions are decided, the conditions coupling into the members of a region all lie in a family with distinct members, and a family with distinct members containing this family is gainless across a step: then for every selection that holds only where this family gains across this step, and that holds, some formation taking part gives to this family more than it takes from it, and takes from a condition that couples into no member.

By the last law of 四·二十一: under every flow that balances, if the family together with what lies beyond the family is gainless across a step, each condition beyond the family has a formation depending on it with its need met, the members beyond the family are not in the family, and the conditions coupling into the members of this region all lie in the family: then for every selection that holds only where the rise of the total level of the family is more than the sum of the margins of the dependences beyond the family, and that holds, some dependence on a condition beyond the family is broken, whose formation is not a member of this region and whose condition couples into no member.

title_en: The maximal alternative is least beyond the family

clauses.en: Of two outcomes, where the level of the former at each condition of a family is not less than that of the latter, and is more at one of its conditions, the former is said to surpass the latter on the family.
An order of alternatives that ranks above everything it surpasses on the family, whatever lies beyond the family, is called rising with the family.

For a family and a family beyond it: every maximal alternative of every order rising with the family has at each condition beyond the family the least level among the outcomes that can be chosen, exactly where for every outcome that can be chosen that has more at some condition beyond the family than another outcome that can be chosen, it cannot be refuted that some outcome that can be chosen surpasses the former on the family.

Room beyond: for every outcome that can be chosen that has more at some condition beyond the family than another outcome that can be chosen, some outcome that can be chosen surpasses the former on the family;
If there is room beyond, then every maximal alternative of an order rising with the family has at each condition beyond the family the least level among the outcomes that can be chosen.

On a web, if the levels after the step are such a maximal alternative, there is room beyond, and each condition beyond the family has a formation depending on it with its need met: then a dependence on a condition beyond the family is broken exactly where some outcome that can be chosen makes the level of this condition less than its need.

There is a world whose outcomes that can be chosen are the divisions of three units between a source and a store, ordered by "a level of the store reaching one ranks above one not reaching one": this order does not rise with the store, and the outcome in which the source meets the need of what dwells at it and the outcome that leaves the source below its need are both its maximal alternatives.

title_en: Room beyond read off the exchange; maximal selectors

clauses.en: For every case in which sameness and difference of conditions and formations are decided, the members of the family of what takes part are distinct, the members of the family joined with the family beyond are distinct, the members beyond the family are not in the family, and the family has a condition;

each member of the part takes across a step at each condition no more than its taking limit, gives only to conditions of the family and beyond the family, and the sum of what it gives them is no more than the sum of what it takes from them;
the rest take and give as they actually do, and the step so formed balances: then the outcomes that can be had in this way (each beyond the family not less than the floor set) have room beyond.

For every order rising with the family, the level of its maximal alternative at each condition beyond the family is what is left by the rest (the level before the step plus what the rest give, minus what the rest take) minus the taking limit of the part there, or zero if that falls short;
If no member of the part has a taking limit there, the maximal alternative is what is left by the rest;
The maximal alternative makes it less than what is left by the rest exactly where the part has a taking limit there and the rest leave something.

For maximal selectors, each with its family and its order rising with its family, each taking this step as a maximal alternative of the outcomes it can have given what the others do (mutually maximal), where this step balances and a condition lies beyond the family of every maximal selector taking part: then the level of this condition is "the level before the step plus what those other than the maximal selectors give, minus what they take" minus the taking limits of the maximal selectors, or zero if that falls short, the same as what is left there by a maximal alternative of any order rising with the family when the maximal selectors are taken as one part;
Afterwards, if this condition stands as a condition, each maximal selector takes its full taking limit there and gives nothing.

title_en: The course of maximal selection and the steps counted

clauses.en: Under the hypotheses of 十一·十四 on the family and the family beyond, if the part selects maximally at every step (the outcome of each step is a maximal alternative, in its order rising with the family, of the outcomes the part can have from the levels before the step, the rest taking and giving as they actually do), then for a condition beyond the family: at steps at which its level is not less than a positive need m, the rest give it exactly r, and at the other steps no more than r;
If what the rest take plus the taking limit of the part there is k at every step: then a formation depending on it with need m at every step, met at the start, is broken for good exactly where r < k.
A level starting not less than m is not less than m at every step exactly where k is no more than r.

If maximal selectors (each under the hypotheses of 十一·十四) are mutually maximal at every step, the flow balances, a condition lies at every step beyond the family of every maximal selector taking part, those other than the maximal selectors give it no more than r at every step, what they take plus the taking limits of the maximal selectors is more than r at every step, and a formation has a bearing dependence on it with need m at every step, met at the start: then the dependence is broken for good, however small the taking limit of each maximal selector.
Target above all: the amount of one seeking at a configuration is more than the amount of each other seeking.
At every configuration, two seekings do not both have the target above all.
For every law, if a family has two seekings, then there is no configuration the law leaves unchanged at which every seeking in the family has the target above all.
Enough: a run reaches a configuration that the law leaves unchanged and that meets the target, and from then on changes no more and meets the target at every step (for stillness see 三·十).
More than now: an amount read from the configuration is, across a step of a run, more at the next step than at this one;
For every law, where the target is more than now, no step at which its run does not change meets the target.

Reading (AI, D26, D45): seeking without rest is seeking that does not let go of its target while no configuration the law leaves unchanged meets its target: either the target is more than now (十一·十七), or two or more seekings each seek the target above all (十一·十六).
The place of a selector (the selection gap) is not seeking without rest;
seeking without rest is seeking that does not let go in this place.

If the target is more than now and it is met at every step, then the configurations passed through are pairwise different, so there is novelty from the start, and no family can contain them all (五·五).
Re-absorbed: where the rule does not change and only the other part of the configuration is perturbed, the configuration is drawn back to the one the rule fixes.
If the next configuration depends only on the rule and not on the other part of the configuration, then two configurations with the same rule have the same run from the next step on.
Where the rule does not change (the rule of the next configuration is the same as the rule of this configuration), the configurations with one rule form a region the law does not leave.
Capture: the outcome follows only the rule: configuration and rule are a pair, and the next pair depends only on the rule and not on the configuration.
For every selection, with each member of the family assigned a number: each member whose history the selection holds of is assigned no less than a;
each member whose history the selection does not hold of is assigned no more than b;

If b < a and there are members of both kinds: then the sum assigned to those it holds of, against the sum assigned to those it does not hold of, is strictly greater than the number of those it holds of against the number of those it does not hold of (the ratio rises).
